667.t: Listening to their old records and Cy Coleman
667.s: They seldom listen to their records; it led to re-recording 'East of Suez' and a Berlin DJ's interest in the Cy Coleman album.
667.ch: Time and Love and later records
667.q: But actually when you walk into somebody’s house and they think that you’ll enjoy it, you know, and it’s really nice that they have them and that they play them, but all of a sudden you don’t hear any conversation, you’re listening to it.

323.t: Remaking Czardas and Hora Staccato; Brahms quintet
323.s: Rerecording faster seven years later, plus the live 1964 Brahms quintet.
323.q: I have to tell you this story. JoAnn, you know it. “Saxophone Contrasts” I recorded Czardas Monti and Hora Staccato. Both excellent. Even I like it. Now I want you to understand what that means, even I like it. That is not egotism, that’s perfectionism. When I say even I like it, I’m very…

576.t: Hating to listen to her own recordings
576.s: She rarely listens to her own records and recently revisited the Blue Note album.
576.q: But just recently I did listen to Blue Note, the Blue Note recording. Because everybody was telling me, giving me really beautiful compliments on it, and I thought gee, what’s the big deal? I don’t — how come I don’t hear it? I don’t hear that. That doesn’t sound good to me. I mean I remember how I…

486.s: Humiliations on recordings and a rough count of about 70 records.
486.q: I can’t really think about it. I mean I can think of some scenes I had with various musicians but nothing — I mean I can think of humiliations I suffered, of my own making. Like this one record I was on I would love to burn. I won’t tell you what it was. Two actually. I just — one I hadn’t touched…

343.t: Why he was chosen so often as a bassist; hearing a 1977 record
343.s: McBee calls himself his worst critic and tells of his wife playing a 1977 record he didn't recognise as himself; music is his therapy.
343.q: Well let me put it this way: I’m my worst, I’ve been over the years, my worst critic. It continued. Until recently I never could appreciate what I’ve done. There’s always more and more that I could learn. And I don’t see that romantically, that’s realistic, you know, reality and so forth. But last…

415.t: Hearing himself on TV and records; Hank Jones
415.s: TV ads, not listening to his records, leaving rough edges, and Hank Jones albums.
415.q: Oh, great guy, and a genius at the piano, really. A giant. A complete piano player, really.

702.s: He mostly avoids hearing himself but can live with a few records.
702.ch: Studio work, recordings and Saturday Night Live
702.q: Some of them. Some of them I don’t, but I always feel like man I don’t want to hear that. I hear my flaws and I know what my strengths and weaknesses are. We all have them. You know naturally when I don’t hear something come out the way I’d like it to it bothers me. So I don’t usually listen to…

108.t: Alec Wilder's sonata album and not listening to his own recordings
108.s: Wilder tells of the Alec Wilder sonata album, not realizing Jim Marr wrote the liner notes, and says he is too critical to replay his recordings.
108.q: I guess you’ve got a point there. I have some of them like this that are still in the cellophane. In fact, what recording was it, oh I did a classical album, Alec Wilder wrote a sonata for me. He had a knack of writing concerti and sonatas and things for his friends you know. And he really puts you…

566.t: Never listening to her own records
566.s: Humes never plays her own records and always feels they could have been better, though she hears playbacks in the studio and asks to sing again.
566.q: No, never. When I came here I sent out my albums, you know, and she put them on and I said, 'is that my record?' She said, yes. I said, 'well I like this one'. She said, now don't tell me you haven't heard it. I said, 'I heard none of them. I never listen to my records'. I don't know, I always feel…

418.t: Which of his records he likes best
418.s: He cannot pick a favorite record but likes two of his own, disliking the response vocal added to one.
418.ch: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
418.q: I couldn't tell you, really. I really couldn't tell you. There's a few that I did like, but I couldn't put no thing on any particular one. I kind of

97.t: Last record; hearing the sections; not a songwriter
97.s: Scott last recorded with Alex Jackson and loved hearing a band.
97.q: Well, the last that I can recall was Alex Jackson. In Alex Jackson's band. Because I'd (unintelligible) before them, but after that there wasn't any -- I wasn't with the record-making --
